title: Tablewright
tagline: Seat 50 guests in seconds: simulated annealing untangles couples, cliques and feuds
problem: Anyone planning a wedding, gala or team dinner ends up shuffling sticky notes for hours, trying to keep couples side by side, friend groups together and feuding relatives far apart. With 50 guests and 7 tables there are more possible arrangements than atoms in the universe, so every manual fix breaks something else. Spreadsheets and drag-and-drop planners only record a plan; they never tell you whether a better one exists.
audience: Couples planning a wedding, event organisers and anyone who has to seat a room full of people with opinions.
solution: Tablewright turns your guest list and a few plain-language rules (sit next to, same table, keep apart) into a cost function, then runs simulated annealing in your browser to search millions of seat swaps for the arrangement with the fewest conflicts. You watch the floor plan rearrange itself live while red conflict lines disappear, then pin anyone you want fixed, fine-tune by hand and export the final chart.
how_it_works: Every rule becomes a weighted penalty: a couple split across tables costs 100, a couple at the same table but not adjacent costs 6, two people who must be kept apart sharing a table costs 100, and splitting a friend group costs 2 per pair.
The plan is a flat array of seats; round-table adjacency is seat i and seat i plus or minus one, wrapping around the table.

Simulated annealing proposes swapping two random seats (including empty ones), computes the cost change from only the rules touching those two guests, and accepts worse moves with probability e^(-delta/T) so it can escape local traps.
The temperature cools geometrically from 60 to 0.05 over hundreds of thousands of swaps, run in small batches per animation frame so the UI stays smooth and you can watch it converge.
The best arrangement seen is kept and restored at the end; pinned guests never move.
features: Live animated floor plan: guests glide between round tables while conflict lines turn from red to gone
Plain-language rules: sit next to, same table, keep apart, plus automatic friend-group cohesion
Harmony score, rules met, hard conflicts and a live convergence chart of the search
Click a guest to see their rules, swap them with anyone by hand, or pin them to a seat
Bulk guest entry (one 'Name, Group' per line), adjustable table count and seats per table
Export as CSV or copy a clean table-by-table list, with a print-friendly layout
Everything autosaves in your browser; nothing leaves your device
tech_highlights: Simulated annealing written from scratch with O(rules per guest) incremental delta scoring, so 300,000 swaps take well under two seconds
Typed arrays for seat and position maps, plus a stamp array to deduplicate shared rules in each delta without allocating
requestAnimationFrame-batched solver with a fixed frame budget so the animation length is the same for 10 or 300 guests
Keyed SVG guest nodes with CSS transform transitions, giving smooth motion without a framework
Zero dependencies: plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript with localStorage persistence
try_it: Open the app: a 50-guest wedding is seated automatically while you watch
Press Shuffle to scramble everyone and see the red conflict lines, then press Solve
Click Uncle Victor, read his rules, and press Pin to lock him in place
Open the Rules tab and add 'Keep apart' between two guests at the same table, then solve again
Export the result as CSV or copy the table list
linkedin_hook: A 50-guest wedding has more seating plans than atoms in the universe, so I let simulated annealing pick one in under two seconds.
